public_rationale: The July 11, 2025 DriveTransformer revision reports results on the simulated Bench2Drive benchmark and the real-world open-loop nuScenes benchmark [e3]. The January 7, 2026 Alpamayo-R1 revision describes a path toward Level 4 autonomous driving [e4]. Neither report establishes a qualifying transformer-based Level 5 deployment or proves that such a system is impossible, leaving the forecast unresolved [e3] [e4].
limitations: The benchmark evaluations do not establish operation across all human-drivable road conditions without human driving or fallback [e3].
The stated path toward Level 4 does not establish Level 5 capability [e4].
These reports do not establish that hallucination makes transformer-based Level 5 driving impossible [e3] [e4].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Transformers will not achieve Level 5 self-driving, because LLMs hallucinate a lot.

statement.excerpt: Transformers (the key technology behind LLMs) won’t get us to Level 5 self-driving; hope springs eternal, but the fact is that LLMs hallucinate a lot.

from_speaker: won’t get us to Level 5 self-driving
our_interpretation: This is an open-ended prediction about achieving Level 5 driving, with hallucination offered as a reason.
Level 5 means performing the driving task under all on-road conditions in which a human can drive, without requiring human driving or fallback.
A qualifying transformer-based system must use transformer models materially to deliver its autonomous driving capability. Incidental transformer use would not suffice.
I do not require transformers to operate without other software, sensors or safety components; the speaker did not specify that restriction.
The hallucination premise is not itself evidence that future Level 5 capability is impossible.
criteria.support_condition: A validated technical impossibility result applying to the claimed class and Level 5 task could support the categorical prediction. Continued lack of deployment cannot establish an unlimited negative forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Public, independently corroborated evidence establishes an operating Level 5 driving system whose autonomous capability materially depends on transformer models.

evidence.explanation: The revised research report documents transformer progress on named driving benchmarks. Simulated closed-loop and real-world open-loop evaluations do not establish unrestricted Level 5 operation.
The revised paper presents reasoning-based driving progress but expressly describes a path toward Level 4. It neither demonstrates Level 5 nor proves that Level 5 is impossible.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Technical documentation and independent operational or regulatory validation of a Level 5 deployment that materially depends on transformers would contradict the forecast. A validated impossibility result covering transformer-based systems and the Level 5 task could support it. Continued lack of deployment cannot settle this unlimited negative forecast.
